test_title: SSC CPO 2023 Official Paper-II (Held On: 08 Jan, 2024)
subject: general
question: What did the early Roman historians use to fill up details in the historical accounts of events?
solution:
The correct answer is** 'Roman and Greek folklore'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage indicates that ancient historians had limited reliable sources of information for early Roman history.
 
• They had a list of annual magistrates (the consular fasti) and religious records and texts of some laws and treaties, which provided only a bare outline of major events.
 
• To flesh out these meagre factual materials, ancient historians supplemented their accounts with folklore.
 
• The passage explicitly states: "Ancient historians fleshed out this meagre factual material with both native and Greek folklore."
 
• This supplementation led to exaggeration, suppression of embarrassing facts, and the invention of details to create more comprehensive narratives.
 
• This use of folklore was necessary to fill in the gaps and provide a more detailed account of Roman affairs.

Therefore, the correct answer is **'Option 1'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The texts of laws and treaties were used to outline major events but did not provide detailed accounts.
 
• Religious records added to the bare outline but did not fill out the historical narrative comprehensively.
 
• The list of annual magistrates (the consular fasti) provided the chronological framework but not detailed event accounts.
